Carbon Re: Reducing carbon emissions by gigatonnes – Cambridge Enterprise
, Buffy Price, Sherif Elsayed-Ali and Dr Aidan O’Sullivan founded Carbon Re with a mission to reduce global emissions at the gigatonne scale, starting with the cement industry.

Specifically designed for the cement pyroprocess, Carbon Re identifies optimisation opportunities in the production process and takes autonomous control of the plant to enact changes. The AI is continually retrained to match actual plant performance, negating the challenge of model drift.

can save plants an average of 5% fuel-derived emissions per year. For an average 2MT plant, that equates to approximately 30,000 tCO2e per year. With 11 clinker-producing plants operating in the UK, Carbon Re could reduce UK CO2 emissions by over half a million tonnes annually.

“We have built a technology that directly reduces CO2 emissions today and is helping the industries that literally support our modern world – cement, steel, glass, transition to a net-zero future. Our mission is to have gigatonnes of impact, starting with kilotonnes of real-world reductions today. With each evolution of our product, we move closer to achieving that goal.”

・Google announces "Gemini 4 Carbon," a new model specialized in coding and cybersecurity. Initially provided only to vetted defensive partners

This new model specializes in the ability to write programs and the ability to find and fix system weaknesses (vulnerabilities). Google explains that compared to previous models, the rate of writing secure code has increased significantly🛡️

However, the ability to find weaknesses can also be used for attacks if used by bad actors. It's what's called "dual-use" (technology that can be used for both good and bad purposes). That's why Google decided not to make it available to everyone, but to provide it to defensive experts first. Pricing and the public release date haven't been announced yet⚡

Drug development is a world where it takes a huge amount of time and money for a single drug to reach the market. Anthropic is trying to use Claude to speed up tasks that get stuck in various parts of the process, not just in molecular design, but also in document checking and manufacturing management 🤖

For example, there are cases where checking thick documents that used to take a person more than a full day can now be finished in a few hours. It also introduces examples where AI helped design antibodies (proteins that work by attaching to foreign substances in the body), leading to improved performance 💡

I consider monopods to be consumables, so I appreciate a lower price. So, I decided to buy it.
It's just a standard twist-lock carbon monopod. Personally, I prefer lever locks, haha.

With twist locks, you can't tell at a glance if they're tightened, or how tight they are. However, the compactness when retracted is overwhelmingly better with the twist-lock style. That part is purely a matter of preference.
The rubber feet on the monopods I've used in the past always seem to go missing for some reason. This one has a green rubber ring that provides resistance, so I don't think it will loosen easily.

The pipe diameter is quite thick, providing excellent stability. I don't see any wobbling. It's stable even when I swing it around with the camera attached. If anything, it might be sturdier than the 290.

Well, it's a monopod, so there's nothing particularly complicated about it. It's sturdy for the price, and I think it's perfectly adequate. I also like the all-black design. (I won't say where, but flashy designs are somehow embarrassing to use.)
